title: When an Optional Supplemental Benefit Rider Begins to Pay for Services
content:
Each of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders charges premium from its effective date but pays for services only once its waiting period has run, and the member is told both dates when the rider is taken.

## The condition

The waiting period the tier fixes has run out, counted in whole months from the rider effective date. Calendar months are counted from the day of the month the rider took effect, a month with no matching day ends on its last day, the final day of the waiting period is itself still inside it, and calendar days are never used in place of calendar months.

The question is settled before the rider is brought into payment, on the rider's own record — its reference, the day it took effect and the basis its waiting period was fixed on — and on that record alone.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical)

On a rider carrying a waiting period of 3 months and a rider effective date falling on the 15th of a month:

- The 15th day of the third month afterwards is **still inside** the waiting period; the final day of the period is itself within it.
- The 16th day of that month is **outside** it, and the rider pays from that day.

On a rider that took effect on the 31st of a month, a third month afterwards having only 30 days ends the waiting period on its last day, the 30th, which is itself still inside the period.

## The two waivers

A member who takes the rider when their medical plan first begins has the waiting period waived on the tiers that waive it, and the rider pays from its effective date.

A member who shows comparable dental, vision or hearing coverage held immediately before, evidenced by a certificate or verified with the earlier carrier, has the waiting period waived; their own recollection of having had coverage opens the enquiry but never waives it by itself.

## Preventive care during the waiting period

Preventive care is not exempt: on a tier with a waiting period even a cleaning is the member's own cost until the period ends, and the plan says so before the appointment rather than after the claim.

## A service given inside the waiting period

A claim for a service given inside the waiting period is denied on the ground that the service fell within the waiting period, and the member is told the date from which the same service would be paid.

## Cancelling and retaking

Cancelling and retaking a rider starts a fresh waiting period; the months already served are not carried over, and the member is warned of this before cancelling.
